own_solution.law: Momentum conservation gives vf = u ln(mi/mfinal). Without payload, vf = 3 ln(3200/800) = 4.158883 km/s. With retained payload q, vf = 3 ln((3200 + q)/(800 + q)) km/s.
assumptions: Classical mechanics is adequate at the stated speeds and precision.
A bolted payload remains attached throughout the burn.
All specified fuel is expelled at the stated constant relative exhaust speed.

notes: All certified answers agree with the rocket equation: retained payloads of 50, 190 and 310 kg give 4.02352, 3.69264 and 3.45377 km/s, respectively. Fuel consumption rate enters both mass evolution and burn duration and cancels for every listed positive rate. The tug payload and previous-flight-only payload have no effect under the stated conditions. Both explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 190 kg and change the payload's attachment. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag because pass 2 identifies T357D and T23F7 as deliberate numeral-free controls, rather than number-preserving minimal pairs; their descriptions accurately identify the removal of the number and unit. The pass-1 numerical answers used m/s and agree with the certified answers after conversion to km/s.
